newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portuguese police chief steps down in row.
newsitem.headline: Portuguese police chief steps down in row.

text.p: Portugal's police chief General Gabriel Teixeira stepped down on Friday in a row over discipline in the force, a police union spokesman said.
Portuguese newspapers say the root of the dispute is in human rights abuses by police.

Domingos Chaves, president of the Professional Association of Public Security Police, told reporters that Teixeira ceased work after presenting proposals which Interior Minister Alberto Costa had requested on Tuesday.
It was not immediately known whether Teixeira had been dismissed. A replacement has not been named so far.
Human rights groups have accused the Portuguese police of committing acts of brutality.

Amnesty International secretary-general Pierre Sane said in a newspaper interview last month that the most serious violations of human rights in Portugal were cases of physical torture and mistreatment by the police.
In November, the European Committee against Torture accused Portuguese police of frequently mistreating people in their custody, saying the most common abuse was blows inflicted with fists or clubs.
